answer: In an agent marketplace managing walnut shipments from an inlet to a wharf, each bidding identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can accept work. Creating 1,000 fake agents therefore ties up $100,000 for a month; splitting one balance among aliases cannot unlock extra bidding slots. Each usable identity requires a separate bond, so an attacker must finance the entire swarm and bear the borrowing cost or lost use of that capital.
